Findings.problem: The trusted insertion promises a u64 outside an arbitrary caller-supplied set, without any availability or allocator-state premise. Choosing all u64 values makes that postcondition impossible for a fresh empty owner; the executable allocator can instead fail when exhausted, so its behavior does not justify this total proof axiom.
Findings.key_premise: The requires at lines 608-615 do not constrain used_ids, while the empty owner constructor at 234-242 supplies list_id == 0; the axiom returns normally and requires a resulting u64 outside used_ids. This is a static contract inconsistency conditional on otherwise valid insertion resources, not a verified claim that those resource premises are inhabitable.
Findings.suggestion: Replace the fresh-ID assumption with an explicit allocator resource and a checked allocation transition that accounts for exhaustion, or require a justified freshness/availability witness and bind the resulting ID to it. Propagate the corrected premise through push and cursor wrappers.

Findings.problem: ListStore defines its intrinsic validity as an inherent method rather than implementing the shared Inv trait. Its many operation contracts already thread this predicate, so the missing trait implementation prevents using the standard invariant abstraction.
Findings.key_premise: The only ListStore invariant definition is in an inherent impl; no Inv implementation for ListStore occurs in the available roots.
Findings.suggestion: Move the unchanged inv definition into impl<M: AnyFrameMeta + Repr<MetaSlotSmall>> Inv for ListStore<M>; retain all existing requirements and preservation clauses.
